THIS CRIMINAL MISC. CASE HAVING BEEN FINALLY HEARD ON 24.03.2026, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY PASSED THE FOLLOWING:
 Crl.M.C No.6269 of 2023  2026:KER:26191  -3-  ORDER (Dated this the 24th day of March, 2026) This is a petition filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, by the accused in Crime No.502 of 2022 of Karamana Police Station, which is pending as CP. No.9 of 2023 on the file of Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-I,
Thiruvananthapuram.

The offences alleged against the petitioner are under Sections 376(1),
376(2)(n), 450, 506(ii) and 420 IPC and Section 66E of IT Act.

2. The prosecution case is that the accused, after promising to marry the de facto complainant,
subjected her to sexual abuse repeatedly and thereafter refused to marry her and thereby, he is alleged to have committed the aforesaid offences.
3.

According to the petitioner, the dispute has been amicably settled with the defacto complainant/victim/ respondent No.2 and that she agreed to drop all further proceedings relating to the above dispute.
Therefore, the petitioner prayed for quashing all further proceedings against him.
4. The de facto complainant/victim filed affidavit endorsing the averments in the Criminal MC.
According to her, the case has 2026:KER:26191 been amicably settled and that she does not intend to proceed with the case and also that further proceedings in the case can be quashed.
She has no further grievance against the petitioner.

5. The learned Public Prosecutor, after getting instruction from the investigating officer also submitted that the dispute has been amicably settled between the parties and that the victim is not interested in continuing the prosecution against the petitioner.

6. On a perusal of the FI statement, it can be seen that the petitioner and the de facto complainant had sexual relationship with each other repeatedly at different places and as such, prima facie, it is revealed that the relationship between them was a consensual one.
7.

Considering the fact that the offences involved in this case are not heinous and very serious, but purely of private in nature and now the dispute has been settled between the parties, quashment of the same is necessary for maintaining harmonious relationship between the parties and also to prevent abuse of process of the court.

Vijith vs State Of Kerala on 24 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6078572/

8. In the result, this Crl. M.C is allowed.

All further proceedings against the petitioner in CP. No.9 of 2023 on the file of Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-I, Thiruvananthapuram, 2026:KER:26191 arising from Crime No.502 of 2022 of Karamana Police Station, is quashed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
